To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a hierarchical inference machine that iterates over a series of learned inference procedures is a powerful and efficient tool for parsing scenes, 2) a single inference machine can be trained to process multiple modalities of data, and 3) a hierarchical inference procedure that iterates over learned inference procedures can be used to process continuous streams of data.

1) we can use an approximate inference procedure as a black box to learn to parse scenes, 2) we can use a learned inference procedure to parse scenes from images, 3) we can use the same learned procedure to parse scenes in 3 D, and 4) the learned procedure can parse scenes from multiple modalities.

1) a hierarchical model for scene parsing that iteratively predicts labels and contextual cues can achieve state of the art performance on standard scene parsing datasets; and, 2) this model can be used to efficiently parse scenes in real time on board real world robots.
